targets.approach: This north-facing buttress in the Gore Range can be reached two ways. The simpler way starts at the Rock Creek trailhead, follows the Freya Tower approach, and then drops southeast into the valley below to the buttress. The other follows the Gore Range Trail south to the bridge over South Rock Creek, then bushwhacks west up the creek past meadows and small outcrops to the base. The route starts at a small rock pillar at the foot of the climb, directly beneath the obvious offwidth on the second pitch.
targets.name: Feel The Rain On Your Skin

targets.approach: Park in the pullout along Mount Blue Sky Road and go down the gully, then follow the Abyss Lake trail south-southwest toward the wall's base. Looking northwest from the stretch between Helms Lake and Lake Fork, the wall is hard to miss; no maintained path leaves the trail for the base, so tread lightly on the tundra. The route begins in the loose chimney of Right of Passage, then breaks left onto the face before the chimney ends, passing left of the crux roof.
targets.descent_text: Walk off to climber's right via obvious grassy ledges, with perhaps a fourth-class move or two.
targets.name: Coming of Age

targets.approach: Trails from the Glacier Gorge trailhead lead to Black Lake. At Stoneman Pass, go east along the divide's south side toward Chiefshead to the conspicuous tower, walk beyond it, and descend northward. Downclimb north to the tower's east side, then use third- and fourth-class ground to swing round to the northeast side and enter a gully. Belay anywhere; climbing to near the summit makes the belay simpler.
targets.name: The Stoneman

targets.approach: The approach goes up Elk Creek to the trail into the Vestal drainage and continues east past a lake, over a pass between two high points. There is good camping with views of the north faces near the tarns, and an obscure trail at the tarn level contours toward the southeast ridge. The route gains the broad northeast ridge and follows it: easier ground first, then a narrowing ridge to the base of a tower that holds the crux.
targets.name: Northeast Ridge

targets.approach: Park at the pulloff by the sheep sign just past the eighteenth highway marker and follow the Hero Traverse east to the Corinthian Column. Turn left there and head down toward the Bottomless Pit, hugging skier's left. At the base of the ridge is a short buttress with several splitter cracks for the first pitch. The ridge runs up out of the pit and joins the Hero Traverse, where you can bail to the right or continue.
targets.name: Hero Ridge
targets.peak: Sunshine Wall & The Buttress Below It

targets.approach: Leave the car at Summit Lake and use the climbers' trail on Spaulding, the same start as for the Black Wall. Cross the top of the Black Wall and go a little farther until a ramp-and-ledge system shows on your right; drop packs at the head of it and downclimb the ramp to the foot of the buttresses. The route begins on a broken pillar beside Noth'N But a Good Time (to its right), then follows a prominent right-leaning ramp system toward the middle meadow of the wall.
targets.name: The Gimp Route

targets.approach: Take the approach to the Rolling Stones Wall, then keep going east along the fence line to the escarpment edge and south to the slot that separates the main cliff from The Citadel. Bachelor Pizza climbs the north face of The Citadel from the base of the approach rappel, which goes down the slot from a bolted anchor with chains. It works as a handy way up to the tower's top, from where the south-face routes are rappelled.
targets.name: Bachelor Pizza

targets.approach: Take the approach to the Rolling Stones Wall, then keep going east along the fence line to the escarpment edge and south to the slot that separates the main cliff from The Citadel. This one-pitch line goes up the left-facing corner to the right of Jimmy Bucket, then a hand crack on the face farther right, and ends at the two-bolt anchor that Texas Wheelchair's third pitch shares.
targets.name: Dalton's Dastardly Dihedral

targets.approach: Take the Rolling Stones Wall approach and go down the gully on its north side to a bolted slab that faces south at a low angle. A second way in is to climb Bachelor Pizza, on The Citadel's north face, and rappel that line. The first pitch is a bolted slab to an anchor on a large ledge, and the line continues up a pillar beside a bolted dihedral.
targets.descent_text: Rappel the route itself, or use the chains at the top to make one rappel down the tower's north face.
targets.name: Tempest

targets.approach: Approach as for Tempest, by way of the Rolling Stones Wall and the gully north of it. This variation shares the lower pitches of Tempest and then diverges right from the big grassy ledge, avoiding the steep roof and staying on easier ground.
targets.descent_text: Descend as for Tempest: rappel the route, or take the chains at the top for a rappel down the tower's north face.
targets.name: Tempest in a Teapot

targets.approach: Take the approach to the Rolling Stones Wall, then keep going east along the fence line to the escarpment edge and south to the slot that separates the main cliff from The Citadel. This line is on the south face: drop down the gully north of the Rolling Stones Wall to a ledge beneath that wall. It climbs moderate runout ground on small gear, then steep cracks and a corner, and finishes in a blocky chimney.
targets.name: Texas Wheelchair

targets.approach: Follow any Sneffels north face approach, continue southwest up the drainage to the pinnacles at its head, and reach their north side by scrambling a rock buttress to the right and an orange ledge. Climb the talus gully to the notch dividing The Hand from The Penguin, then make an easy third-class scramble up and right to the clear east crack.
targets.descent_text: Either rappel the crack, or walk around to the west side and downclimb loose fourth-class ground into the Penguin-Thumb saddle.
targets.name: East Crack

targets.approach: Follow any Sneffels north face approach, continue southwest up the drainage to the pinnacles, and reach their north side via a rock buttress and an orange ledge. The sharp saddle between The Penguin and The Thumb is gained through the north talus gully or from The Penguin itself; then work west up the slopes until the angle kicks up. The route follows a shallow depression on the southeast face.
targets.descent_text: Sling or build an anchor in the plentiful cracks and rappel back down to the approach slopes.
targets.name: Southeast Face

targets.approach: Leave the car at the lot by the sixteenth highway marker and walk east to the ridge's high point. Locate the gash in the south side and The Blade. Hiking down the Dinosaur Couloir and scrambling up to the base is possible, but rappelling in has less effect on the terrain and the sheep; the anchors are set in a groove behind the top-out, with another farther down and to skier's right, and the gully below leads around to the base. The route starts on the left side of the formation, aiming for a laser-cut fist crack.
targets.name: Katana Ridge

targets.approach: Leave the car at the lot by the sixteenth highway marker and walk east up to the ridge. Two ways lead in. One uses the Katana Ridge rappels, then crosses broken ledges beyond its base to the grassy ledges below the first pitch. The other rappels in from this route's top, a short way over to the skier's right from Katana Ridge's summit, at a roomy ledge split by a wide crack in a dihedral. The route is on the left of The Wall, following a thin dihedral system into the conspicuous wide crack.
targets.name: The Wakizashi Cracks

targets.approach: The route starts on the ledge above the anchor for The Nose and just right of Bartertown. Climb The Nose to its bolted anchor on the ledge, then head up and left to the next ledge and begin the roofs and corner above.
targets.name: Pursuit Special

targets.approach: Start at the Slavonia trailhead, take the Gilpin Lake trail until it meets Trail 1162, which climbs into Mica Basin, and hike up to Mica Lake. The crag sits beneath Big Agnes Mountain, east and a little north of the lake: go northeast, descend below a steep overhanging crag, and continue northeast for a short way. A band of pale quartzite crosses the face diagonally, giving the crag its name. The route starts on the right side of that white stripe in the black granite, up a slab where a left-leaning undercling crack leads off.
targets.name: Seven Nation Army
